title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice on the Jurisdiction over Criminal Cases Involving Foreigners
keywords_en: jurisdiction; Ministry of Justice on criminal cases of foreigners
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate

Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, Ministry of Justice

Notice on Issues Concerning the Jurisdiction over Criminal Cases Involving Foreigners

Fa Fa [2013] No. 2

To: the High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), State Security Departments (Bureaus), and Justice Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and the People's Procuratorate, Public Security Bureau, State Security Bureau, and Justice Bureau of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

For the purpose of implementing and properly applying the provisions on jurisdiction over criminal cases under the amended Criminal Procedure Law, ensuring the quality of handling criminal cases involving foreigners, and taking into account the characteristics of such cases and the practical needs of case handling, the relevant matters concerning jurisdiction over criminal cases involving foreigners are hereby notified as follows:

1. First-instance criminal cases involving foreigners shall, except for those provided for in Articles 20 to 22 of the Criminal Procedure Law, be under the jurisdiction of basic people's courts. In regions where there are a large number of criminal cases involving foreigners, the intermediate people's court may designate one or several basic people's courts within its jurisdiction to exercise centralized jurisdiction over first-instance criminal cases involving foreigners. In regions where there are few criminal cases involving foreigners, the intermediate people's court may, in accordance with Article 23 of the Criminal Procedure Law, try first-instance criminal cases involving foreigners that are under the jurisdiction of basic people's courts.

2. Investigation of criminal cases involving foreigners shall be conducted by the public security organ or state security organ at the place where the crime was committed or where the criminal suspect resides. Where it is necessary to arrest a criminal suspect, the public security organ or state security organ responsible for the investigation shall request approval of the arrest from the people's procuratorate at the same level at the place where the investigation authority is located. Where, upon completion of the investigation, a case needs to be transferred for review and prosecution, it shall be transferred to the people's procuratorate at the same level as the investigating authority. Where the people's procuratorate receives a case transferred by the investigating authority at the same level for review and prosecution, and, in accordance with the jurisdictional provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law and the requirements of this Notice, considers that the case should be prosecuted by a higher-level people's procuratorate or by another people's procuratorate at the same level, it shall transfer the case to the people's procuratorate with jurisdiction for review and prosecution.

3. A basic people's court within the jurisdiction exercising centralized jurisdiction over first-instance criminal cases involving foreigners shall be proposed by the intermediate people's court in consultation with the people's procuratorate, public security bureau, state security bureau, and justice bureau at the same level, after comprehensive consideration of factors such as case handling quality, efficiency, and coordination of work. Such designation shall be determined upon obtaining the consent of the high people's court, provincial people's procuratorate, provincial public security department (bureau), provincial state security department (bureau), and provincial justice department (bureau), and shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice for record.

All high people's courts, provincial people's procuratorates, public security departments (bureaus), and state security departments (bureaus) shall earnestly strengthen supervision and guidance over the work of basic people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and state security organs in handling criminal cases involving foreigners. Judicial administrative organs shall strengthen guidance and supervision over the work of defense counsel and representatives in criminal cases involving foreigners. Significant issues concerning the application of law that arise shall be promptly reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice.

January 17, 2013
